weekly.title: Weekly AI signal brief
weekly.summary: Cross-source evidence is grouped into inspectable themes. Open a theme to review the underlying public sources.

themes.name: AI-native GTM
themes.definition: AI systems that execute or coordinate prospecting, sales, marketing, customer intelligence, and revenue operations.

themes.name: Small & specialized models
themes.definition: Compact or task-specific models optimized for cost, latency, privacy, or a narrow operational decision.

themes.name: Operational ontology
themes.definition: A governed semantic layer connecting business objects, relationships, rules, and actions for people and agents.

themes.name: Frontier inference infrastructure
themes.definition: Large-scale clusters, serving systems, networks, and operational designs built primarily for frontier-model inference.

themes.name: Specialized inference silicon
themes.definition: Chips and computer architectures designed specifically to reduce the latency, energy, or cost of model inference.

themes.name: Agent harnesses
themes.definition: Control systems around models that manage planning, tools, state, execution, recovery, and multi-agent coordination.

themes.name: Assurance infrastructure
themes.definition: Evaluation, security, observability, permissions, governance, and provenance required to operate AI systems safely.

themes.name: Open, local & efficient inference
themes.definition: Open-weight, quantized, on-device, and efficiency-focused approaches that reduce dependence on hosted frontier APIs.

themes.name: Model routing & heterogeneous stacks
themes.definition: Systems that select or combine models according to task, cost, latency, capability, privacy, or reliability requirements.

themes.name: Training, evaluation & self-improvement
themes.definition: Methods and systems that improve model or agent performance through training, feedback, evaluation, optimization, or generated experience.

themes.name: Coding agents & developer tooling
themes.definition: AI systems that search repositories, write and review code, run tools, validate changes, and participate in software delivery.

themes.name: Validation & release infrastructure
themes.definition: Testing, review, runtime validation, and deployment controls that determine whether AI-generated work is safe to release.

themes.name: Multimodal generation & 3D
themes.definition: Systems that generate, edit, understand, or reconstruct images, video, spatial scenes, avatars, and three-dimensional environments.

themes.name: Voice & audio interfaces
themes.definition: Speech recognition, synthesis, cloning, audio generation, and real-time voice systems used as human or agent interfaces.

themes.name: Skills, protocols & integrations
themes.definition: Reusable capabilities, connectors, protocols, and application interfaces that let models and agents act beyond a chat session.

themes.name: Documents, retrieval & knowledge systems
themes.definition: Parsing, retrieval, structured generation, graphs, and data systems that make private or complex information usable by AI workflows.

themes.name: Memory & context engineering
themes.definition: Techniques for selecting, compressing, persisting, and retrieving context across long-running model or agent activity.

themes.name: Enterprise & vertical AI
themes.definition: AI products adapted to industry workflows, governed organizational data, and live business systems.

themes.name: Web & browser automation
themes.definition: Agent capabilities for navigating websites, collecting permitted web data, operating forms, and executing browser-based workflows.

themes.name: Robotics & embodied AI
themes.definition: Models, datasets, simulations, and control systems that connect learned intelligence to physical sensing and action.

themes.name: Governed proprietary-data boundaries
themes.definition: Architectures that keep proprietary, regulated, or customer-confidential data inside controlled systems while exposing only permitted context or computation to models.

evidence.title: Show HN: Made an open-source Lego AI generator
evidence.summary:
Hi there :-) New on HN, first time posting.

Past year, around December, I started experimenting with making ChatGPT and Claude generate source code in LDraw language.

This LDraw is literally an "assembly" language, a low-level programming language that describes how to assemble LEGO pieces together into models, one placement instruction at a time.

When executed by specific tools, like e.g. LDView, LeoCAD, Studio... these instructions become LEGO CAD models, that can be interacted with, modified, etc.

Or, in other words: one LDraw source file in .mpd or .ldr format is equivalent to one LEGO CAD model.

So, the idea I had was: if I manage for maybe ChatGPT or Claude to generate high-quality LDraw source files... then, they would actually be generating high-quality LEGO CAD models, right?

Then, after months of iterations and trying one thing after the other... it worked!!!

Long story short: using GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5, I've managed to create a python toolset, instructions, and docs for agents in general. Now, these can be used by them to generate LDraw models.

evidence.title: Show HN: S3-Accelerator
evidence.summary:
s3-accelerator is an s3-compatible nvme cache that serves hits in under a millisecond, replicates hot objects, and stays warm when the cluster resizes.

the hot object replication was inspired by groupcache [1], but that has some pretty nasty issues when the cluster resizes

s3-accelerator fixes that by: 1) using rendezvous hashing to reduce the remapping when the cluster loses a node, and 2) when new nodes are added, asking the old parent for a give key for the object rather than going to s3

It also uses learnings from cloudflare that it's better to cache on a second hit than a first hit[2]

It also uses ktls, splice, and sendfile so byte transfer of object chunks never hit userspace. That means it can hit millions of iops, or saturate 200Gb/s network cards, while sipping on CPU

it also is parquet-aware, and has an optional SQS integration to keep the cache fresh if an object is overwritten.

S3 stays the source of truth, and you can write through the cache (it wont cache the write by default)

these features make s3-accelerator uniquely performant, fresh, and s3 costs extremely low.

evidence.title: Show HN: Thoreau BASIC – What if BASIC hadn't gone out of fashion?
evidence.summary:
Thoreau BASIC started as a joke. I wanted a BASIC where I could type something ridiculous like:

 DIM A%(12000000000)
…and have it actually work. Then I kept adding things. The result is Thoreau BASIC, a free x64 BASIC interpreter inspired by GW-BASIC, running both as a normal Windows program and directly on bare-metal UEFI without an operating system.

Version 3.2 has become considerably more ambitious than the little interpreter I originally intended to write. The language still deliberately looks and feels like old Microsoft BASIC. Line numbers, GOTO, GOSUB, PRINT, PSET, LINE, CIRCLE, DRAW, etc. are all there. But underneath that rather innocent-looking surface is now quite a lot of machinery.

evidence.title: Show HN: Zebu - time tracking/invoicing for freelancers and small teams
evidence.summary:
Zebu is a time tracking and invoicing app for freelancers and small teams. It's €5 per seat per month (billed yearly), flat, with no usage fees. There's a limited free plan for solo use.

I built it after 15 years as a solo freelancer on Harvest. After they were acquired, my renewal exploded from $12/month to ~$180/month, and unclear usage based pricing made it hard to predict how much it would always cost. The BBC even reported customers seeing increases of 1,500% - https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyq011414eo.

I've been working on a replacement for the past year, and am happy to say my colleagues and I now use it full-time. In many ways it even surpasses the featureset I'd had on Harvest - it's really kind of amazing what kind of custom tooling one can build these days.

I'd especially like feedback on how the migration is working from any services you might come from, any critical integrations that might be useful, and especially what might be missing for team use.

evidence.title: Tell HN: Uceprotect is extorting website owners
evidence.summary:
I recently discovered by accident that our website was being blocked by Orange's security filters.

After a quick check, I found that our IP address is listed on UCEPROTECT Level 3. The listing is based on the reputation of the entire ASN 14061 (DigitalOcean, US) [1]. In other words, even if your IP did nothing wrong, it will still be listed because of its ASN.

If your site is innocent and listed only because it's hosted on DigitalOcean, UCEPROTECT offers to whitelist it for about $30/month or $108/year [2].

I checked the ASNs of several other popular hosting providers, and they're all listed too. So if your site is hosted on DigitalOcean or any other major provider, it's probably blacklisted as well. That can cut you off from customers on mobile networks like Orange, whose "cybersecurity protection" uses blacklists like UCEPROTECT to filter traffic.

Honestly, in my 20-year career, this is the first time I've seen a blacklist misbehave this badly and ask for money when there's clearly been no wrongdoing.

Hi HN, I'm Hongyin. I built Vibivibi (https://vibivibi.com) because I kept starting a coding agent session on my laptop and wanting to continue it on a server, or hand it to a colleague. I want an easier way to do it but won’t trust anyone hosting my traces who promises they won’t sell it (market price per coding trace is $50 to $100).

What Vibivibi does: a small CLI, `vibi`, finds the sessions your coding agents keep locally (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Pi), encrypts one on your machine and uploads it. On another machine `vibi pull` puts it back where the agent expects it, so `claude --resume <id>` just continues. `vibi push` can also send a session to someone else by email.

evidence.summary:
Soldstack is a site for developers to get the buy or sell value of a product mainly on Poshmark right now.

The reason I built this is because eBay sold data got locked behind a login, and Poshmark data is messy and often over a year old. So I wanted to create something that makes it easier to access this data.

When I was making this, I had to be careful with cleaning out the data. For example, if one searched nike dunk low, they would get nike dunk lows, toddler and kid's sizes (which go much cheaper), bundles, other shoes, duplicates, and high outliers. evidence.title: Show HN: Self-bench – benchmark coding agents on real-world software
evidence.summary:
Hey HN,

Today, we're launching selfbench.dev, an open-source tool that lets you create and run evals automatically from your PRs.

Every benchmark with sufficient trust eventually gets benchmaxxed (Goodhart's law) - the labs are incentivized to maximize their scores on that benchmark, which isn't predictive on whether it'll actually work within your setup. This has been a time-consuming process that only the largest companies can afford to do, so we built self-bench to fix this.

Self-bench uses agents to author / review Harbor environments generated from your PRs. You then approve every eval that the agent created, and can model/harness evals concurrently on sandboxes.

To save you money, we also allow you to connect your OpenAI and Claude subscriptions so you don't have to pay raw token costs.
